test_title: PYST 15: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following rivers is NOT a major river of the Great Plateau (Peninsular Plateau) of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Yamuna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Yamuna River is a major tributary of the Ganga and flows through the northern plains of India, not the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• The Great Plateau of India, also known as the Peninsular Plateau, is primarily drained by rivers like the Krishna, Godavari, Narmada, and others originating in this region.
 
• The Yamuna originates from the Yamunotri Glacier in the Himalayas and flows through states like Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Delhi.
 
• Rivers of the Peninsular Plateau, such as the Narmada, Godavari, and Krishna, have distinct east-west drainage patterns shaped by the plateau's topography.
 
• The Yamuna is part of the Ganga river basin, which is geographically separate from the rivers of the Peninsular Plateau.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peninsular Plateau Rivers:**

 
 
• The Narmada and Tapti are west-flowing rivers, draining into the Arabian Sea.
 
• The Krishna, Godavari, and Kaveri are east-flowing rivers, draining into the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan vs. Peninsular Rivers:**
 
 
• Himalayan rivers like the Yamuna are perennial and fed by glaciers and rainfall.
 
• Peninsular rivers are mostly rain-fed and have seasonal flow patterns.
 
 
 
• **River Yamuna:**
 
 
• It is the second-largest tributary of the Ganga after the Ghaghara.
 
• Major cities along its course include Delhi, Agra, and Mathura.
 
 
 
• **Drainage Patterns:**
 
 
• Rivers in the Peninsular Plateau exhibit dendritic, radial, and trellis drainage patterns due to the varied topography.
 
• The Narmada River flows in a rift valley, creating a linear drainage pattern.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Separation:**
 
 
• The Peninsular Plateau is bounded by the Vindhya and Satpura ranges in the north, separating it from the plains of northern India.
 
• The Yamuna lies to the north of the Vindhya range, outside the Peninsular Plateau region.
